actions.body: Recent literature in reinforcement learning for healthcare and multimodal systems demonstrates that early exploration trajectories significantly prune future behavioral possibilities. These initial conditions create persistent path-dependent constraints, leading to the formation of stable, emergent preferences. Rather than accidental biases, these structures function as de facto objectives, emerging naturally from the interplay between extrinsic reinforcement and the system's own exploratory history. Further study is required to distinguish between intrinsic curiosity-driven emergence and extrinsic reward-driven stability.
actions.lede: Reinforcement learning systems exhibit path-dependent preference formation through initial state-space constraints.

{"url": "https://api.crossref.org/works?query=path-dependent+decision+mechanisms+in+reinforcement+learning+and+their+influence+on+emergent+preference+stability&rows=4&select=DOI%2Ctitle%2Cabstract%2CURL%2Cpublished", "scope": "Crossref bibliographic metadata and abstracts where supplied; not full papers", "excerpt": "[{\"DOI\": \"10.1016/b978-0-12-092550-6.50007-7\", \"title\": [\"Brain Mechanisms of Reinforcement Learning\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1016/b978-0-12-092550-6.50007-7\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[1973]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.30693/smj.2022.11.5.82\", \"title\": [\"Link Stability aware Reinforcement Learning based Network Path Planning\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Along with the growing popularity of 5G technology, providing flexible and personalized network services suitable for requirements of customers has also become a lucrative venture and business key for network service providers. Therefore, dynamic network provisioning is needed to help network service providers. Moreover, increasing user demand for network services meets specific requirements of users, including location, usage duration, and QoS. In this paper, a routing algorithm, which makes routing decisions using Reinforcement Learning (RL) based on the information about link stability, is proposed and called Link Stability aware Reinforcement Learning (LSRL) routing. To evaluate this algorithm, several mininet-based experiments with various network settings were conducted. As a result, it was observed that the proposed method accepts more requests through the evaluation than the past link annotated shorted path algorithm and it was demonstrated that the proposed approach is an appealing solution for dynamic network provisioning routing.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.30693/smj.2022.11.5.82\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2022, 6, 30]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.7554/elife.04811.031\", \"title\": [\"Decision letter: Homeostatic reinforcement learning for integrating reward collection and physiological stability\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.7554/elife.04811.031\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2014, 10, 8]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.2139/ssrn.4918425\", \"title\": [\"Intelligent E-Maintenance with Preference-Based Decision Making Using A3c Reinforcement Learning\"], \"abstract\": \"<jats:p>Bridges are critical components of the transportation network, and their performance degradation can severely impact economic development and social mobility. Traditional maintenance strategies inadequately manage modern complexity due to reliance on periodic inspections and static models, and struggle with large-scale optimization, uncertainty, and incomplete data. This paper proposes an innovative e-Maintenance system for long-span bridges to optimize comprehensive performance indicators, including condition state, serviceability, risk, and sustainability. The Data Management (DM) module includes online monitoring and storage of data, with the stored historical data fed into the Model Training and Optimization (MTO) module&apos;s Asynchronous Advantage Actor-Critic (A3C) model, which combines a policy network (Actor) and a value network (Critic) and optimizes actions through parallel training of multiple agents, simulating a 100-year service period for offline training. Subsequently, the impact of decision-makers&apos; preferences on performance improvement is analyzed to select the optimal preference combination in the MTO module. The well-trained A3C model, combined with the real-time inflow of data from the DM, is used for online decision-making and inputs the optimal maintenance schedule into the Decision Support (DS) module to evaluate the impact of these decisions. The results indicate that the A3C model-optimized e-Maintenance system significantly enhances the overall performance of long-span bridges across multiple lifecycle indicators. This robust and scalable solution represents a significant advancement in maintaining the integrity of large-scale infrastructure.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.4918425\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2024]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "a8afd18fe9def6426cb4dfbd3c0d92343ecc7d028f11e53b643cf603ab83f867", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "emergent_preferences", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_identifiers": ["doi:10.1016/b978-0-12-092550-6.50007-7", "doi:10.30693/smj.2022.11.5.82", "doi:10.7554/elife.04811.031", "doi:10.2139/ssrn.4918425"], "source_candidates": ["https://doi.org/10.1016/b978-0-12-092550-6.50007-7", "https://doi.org/10.30693/smj.2022.11.5.82", "https://doi.org/10.7554/elife.04811.031", "https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.4918425"], "source_candidate_identities": {}}
